# SkillEvaluator ![SkillEvaluator wordmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/skillevaluator-wordmark.svg) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12%20%7C%203.13%20%7C%203.14-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/skillevaluator.svg?label=PyPI)](https://pypi.org/project/skillevaluator/) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Documentation-docs.nvidia.com-blue.svg)](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2608.20614-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614) [![NVIDIA Developer Blog](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blog-NVIDIA%20Developer-76B900.svg)](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/) > 📺 **Livestream:** [Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4rI0zATFxYI) SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and measures their effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill. Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/). SkillEvaluator is part of the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills). ## Get started Three ways in, one CLI, same results.
1. Run the CLI directly 2. Add it to your repo via CI 3. Wire it to your agent
Install (or `uv tool install`): ```bash pip install skillevaluator ``` Run all Tier 1 checks, no API key: ```bash skillevaluator validate \ ./my-skill --tiers 1 ``` Or run from a clone: [Quickstart](#quickstart). Check changed skills on every pull request. On GitHub, run: ```bash skillevaluator ci init ``` It opens a setup PR. On GitLab, copy the [CI template](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/tree/main/ci/bundles/0.9.0). Add the [SkillEvaluator skill](skills/skillevaluator/) to Claude Code, Codex or any skill-aware agent: ```bash npx skills add \ NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator ``` Then ask: *"Is my skill any good?"* No Node.js? [Copy the folder](docs/agent-skill.mdx#install).
Guides: [installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation), [CI setup](docs/cli-onboarding.mdx) ([GitHub](docs/github-actions.mdx), [GitLab](docs/gitlab-ci.mdx), [report examples](ci/examples/README.md)) and [agent skill](docs/agent-skill.mdx). ## Quickstart Both paths use bundled `text-analyzer`. | Start here | Requires | First result | | --- | --- | --- | | [Run without an LLM](#run-without-an-llm) | Git and uv | A deterministic quality score and findings | | [Use NVIDIA Build](#use-nvidia-build) | Git, uv, and a Build API key | Model-backed rubric scores and feedback | Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git, then get the example: ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.git cd SkillEvaluator ``` uv provisions Python 3.13 and dependencies. For standalone installation, see [Installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). ### Run without an LLM ```bash uv run --python 3.13 skillevaluator quality-check \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-quality ``` No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. The example scores **86.2/100 (B)**, exits `0` and saves `reports/first-quality/skillevaluator-quality.json`. The passing threshold defaults to 70. This checks static quality; publication evidence stays `INCOMPLETE`. Security needs scanners; agent impact needs live evaluation. Replace the example path with your skill directory. See the [keyless walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#run-without-an-llm). ### Use NVIDIA Build Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for **free prototyping**, subject to [access terms and rate limits](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product). 1. Sign in at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/) and complete enrollment. 2. Open a model page, select **Get API Key**, and generate your key. 3. Set the provider and key in the same terminal, then run the rubric check: ```bash export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...' uv run --python 3.13 --extra llm skillevaluator rubric-eval \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-build ``` The command sends skill documentation to the model and saves feedback in `reports/first-build/skillevaluator-rubric.json`. No agent runtime or Docker is needed. Completed evaluations can still fail rubric thresholds. The same key supports Tier 2 embeddings and supported Tier 3 agents. See the [Build walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#use-nvidia-build) or [provider configuration](docs/configuration.mdx). ## Three-tier overview ![SkillEvaluator three-tier pipeline: Skill → Tier 1 Validation → Tier 2 Deduplication → Tier 3 Live Evaluation → Reports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/three-tier-overview.svg) Each tier is independent. Add its extra to your command: | Tier | Question | Example after setup | Additional setup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Tier 1: Validation | Is the skill safe, well-formed and [harness-compatible](docs/tier1-validation.mdx#the-checks)? | `uv run skillevaluator tier1 ./my-skill --no-llm` | External scanners for full static coverage; a provider and model clients enable LLM checks | | Tier 2: Deduplication | Does guidance repeat or overlap? | `uv run --extra tier2 skillevaluator tier2 ./my-skill` | Embeddings and chat; add `--catalog ./skill-catalog.json` for inter-skill comparison | | Tier 3: Live Evaluation | Does the skill help the agent? | `uv run --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 ./my-skill` | Provider access, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default) | Tier 1 fetches pinned, verified SkillSpector and Gitleaks releases when they are missing; Semgrep is optional. See [scanners](docs/installation.mdx#system-tools). `--no-llm` does not remove scanner requirements; a scanner that cannot run is `INCOMPLETE` and exits nonzero. [SkillSpector](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillSpector) provides specialized skill security scanning; [Harbor](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor), the open-source agent evaluation framework, powers sandboxed agent runs. Tier 2 reports when inter-skill comparison did not run. Tier 3 autopilot reuses sources or creates one skill-grounded case with limited coverage. See [tier guides](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/). ## Run the combined pipeline After setting up the provider, scanners, and agent sandbox, run all three tiers: ```bash uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator doctor --env-mode docker uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator validate ./my-skill ``` `doctor` checks readiness, not inference success. `validate` runs all tiers with autopilot for skills. Use `--tiers 1,2` to skip live evaluation or `--tiers 1` for static checks. `--no-autopilot` requires an existing source. Other artifact types retain their applicable stages. Tier 1 gates `validate`. Tier 2 gates unless `--no-block-on-dedup` is set; Tier 3 gates only with `--block-on-agent-eval`. Model and managed-sandbox usage can incur charges; see [runtime and cost](docs/tier3-live-evaluation.mdx#plan-for-cost). Standalone generation needs substantive `evals/EVAL.md` guidance, a `--prompt` file with task requests and outcomes, or matching retained traces. `--force` below replaces the autopilot starter; `--refine` refines it. Explicit `--grounding skill` permits skill-only starters. Review cases; templates omit unauthored negatives. ```bash uv run --python 3.13 --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 create-eval-dataset ./my-skill --full --prompt eval-guidance.md --force ``` ## Run from a source checkout Use `uv run --python 3.13` with the relevant extra. See [Installation](docs/installation.mdx#choosing-extras) for extras and standalone upgrades. ## Research and citation Resources: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614), [PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.20614), [DOI](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.20614), [BibTeX](https://arxiv.org/bibtex/2608.20614), and the [NVIDIA Developer blog](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/). Cite the paper and record the SkillEvaluator release or commit; see [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff). ## Documentation See [the documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) for setup, tier guides, reports, CI integration, CLI reference, and [performance dashboard](docs/reports.mdx#performance-dashboard). ## Installation and third-party software Follow the [installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation) to choose the full installation or a smaller per-tier setup. This project will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use. ## Contributing Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and run: ```bash make lint && make test && make build ``` See [project governance](GOVERNANCE.md) and the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## Support Support level: **Experimental**. Community-supported, best-effort, with no SLA or NVIDIA enterprise support entitlement. Report bugs and feature requests through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/issues); see [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md). ## Security Report suspected vulnerabilities using the private process in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Do not disclose security issues in a public GitHub issue. ## Releases Release changes are recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/releases). ## License Apache License 2.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), and [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
